name: Adaptive Rendering Loss Regularization
aliases: Adaptive Rendering loss regularization for few-shot NeRF
definition: A method for few-shot NeRF that aligns the frequency relationship between Positional Encoding (PE) and pixel supervision. It focuses on learning low-frequency global structures in early training and high-frequency local details later, using two-phase rendering supervision and adaptive rendering loss weight learning.
summary: Adaptive Rendering Loss Regularization is a training strategy for few-shot NeRF that aligns positional encoding frequencies with pixel supervision using two-phase rendering and uncertainty-based loss weighting without external modules.
